answer: An agent economy can anchor identity in a kernel of verifiable useful work: before an agent may transact, it must finish small, randomly assigned tasks whose outputs peers can cheaply check. Each finished task mints a non-transferable onyx credit tied to that agent's key, and credits decay unless the agent keeps doing honest work. A Sybil farmer must pay the real compute and time cost of useful work for every fake identity, while a zephyr-fast identity with no work history earns no credit at all, so spinning up ten thousand sock puppets costs ten thousand times the work of one real agent.
